A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LayerCraft and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite substantial rewriting, reorganization, and replacement of examples.

before.justification: V1 reports original LayerCraft benchmark scores in Table 1 and qualitative generation, editing, and inpainting results throughout the paper and supplement.

after.justification: V2 reports LayerCraft benchmark scores, quantitative CoT ablations in Table 2, and original batch-editing and subject-driven inpainting comparisons.

M1.justification: V2 introduces a specific bounding-box refinement procedure: visualize the proposed box on the image and iteratively adjust its position and size (Appendix 11, Figure 12). V1 describes general output checking without this targeted loop. The three-agent architecture, dual-LoRA OIN, and attention-combination equations remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds batch collage editing with explicit consistency requirements across photographs, demonstrated through shared clothing, necklaces, graduation props, and advertising objects (Figures 1, 5, 7–9). This substantially extends v1's individual-image generation and sequential editing scenarios. IPA300K and T2I-CompBench coverage remain; GenEval results are promised but not supplied.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator set. The matched qualitative T2I comparisons add Show-O, Janus-Pro 7B, LLM Blueprint, GPT-4o, and GenArtist, while removing PixArt-alpha's displayed examples (v1 Figure 6; v2 Figures 4 and 15). V2 also adds ACE++ and EasyControl inpainting comparisons and a modified GenArtist collage comparison.

E3.justification: The new CoT ablations use a stratified 20% test subset, and the collage comparison supplies GenArtist with ground-truth bounding boxes and intermediate prompts. These introduce evaluation controls within retained tasks. The stated backbone, temperature, hardware, 50K training subset size, and training iteration budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds four quantitative CoT ablations separating generation order, object relationships, their combination, and all layout CoT (Table 2). It also tests removal of OIN/intermediate references for clothing consistency and illustrates bounding-box refinement. The attention-mixing alternatives already analyzed in v1 are retained in Appendix 10.1.

E5.justification: Both versions mention four seeds for synthetic dataset creation, but neither reports repeated-evaluation counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's additional quantitative results retain point-score reporting.

E6.justification: All six LayerCraft scores in Table 1 change: color 0.8536 to 0.8643, shape 0.6096 to 0.7046, texture 0.7937 to 0.8147, spatial 0.4735 to 0.6432, non-spatial 0.3106 to 0.3508, and numeracy 0.6354 to 0.6331. Baseline scores remain fixed, changing LayerCraft's reported lead from three columns to all six. V2 adds ablation and qualitative/runtime findings and removes some earlier demonstrations; the PDFs do not explain the Table 1 revisions.

T1.justification: The object-list formulation and OIN equations for separate attention branches, text-token averaging, and masked latent replacement are mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs; v2's additional explanations do not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: V2 makes identity-preserving integration across multiple images and batch collage editing central contributions in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. It also broadens v1's qualified training claims to statements such as 'without retraining' and 'without requiring model finetuning', despite retaining the OIN training procedure.

C2.justification: V2 attributes spatial consistency to particular CoT components and cross-image consistency to intermediate references, supported by new ablations. It adds discussion of difficult LLM bounding-box proposals and replacing OIN with concurrent inpainting models, while removing v1's strong optics-and-mechanics interpretation of object replacement. The computational-overhead limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents aligned background versus biased reference positional embeddings and clarifies LoRA activation in Section 3.3. It resolves the training paragraph's IPA150K/IPA300K naming inconsistency and removes 'upon acceptance' from the promised code release. These changes do not establish a new training corpus or actual code availability.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against multimodal generators, recent autoregressive models, LLM Blueprint, and concurrent subject-driven inpainting methods ACE++ and EasyControl. The discussion now emphasizes cross-image identity preservation and model/adapter reuse against these alternatives, extending the retained LayoutGPT, GenArtist, and OminiControl comparisons.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V2 introduces a standalone ablation section and reorganizes the appendix around batch editing, comparisons, OIN analysis, and bounding-box refinement. Much of the living-room reasoning example is retained and reformatted.

P2.justification: V2 switches from two-column to single-column presentation, redesigns the teaser and qualitative comparison grids, and adds the ablation table and editing/refinement figures. Existing panels are also relocated: v1 OIN Figures 15–16 become v2 Figures 13–14. Several other earlier demonstrations are removed.

improvement.justification: The new CoT ablations in Table 2 and OIN/reference-image comparison in Figure 5 directly test central design choices that v1 supported mainly through demonstrations. Broader editing comparisons also strengthen the evidence. The net gain is limited by unexplained Table 1 score revisions and less-qualified training-free claims that conflict with the retained LoRA training description.
